comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment for Level 3 gains, losses, and securities valuation changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Net realized/unrealized gains and losses for Level 3 assets and liabilities are presented as increases or decreases to those positions. Changes in fair value of available-for-sale debt securities are recorded in AOCI (unless credit impairment), while sales gains/losses go to the Consolidated Statement of Income; unrealized gains/losses on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft (MS) and Citigroup (C) disclose the specific income statement classification for gains and losses on Mortgage Servicing Rights (MSRs). MS classifies gains and losses for 'Loans and Other assets-Other investments' (which includes MSRs) in 'Other revenues'. Similarly, C explicitly states that 'Unrealized gains (losses) on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue'. While MS provides a broader policy for other items (held-for-sale vs. held-for-investment), both firms agree on the treatment of MSR-related fair value changes as flowing through 'Other revenues' rather than other expenses or OCI.

comparisons.peer_topic: Materiality of Fair Value Gains/Losses on Loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Gains or losses from changes in fair value of loans held for investment accounted for under the fair value option were not material in 2024 and 2023, and were included in other principal transactions.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose the income statement placement for fair value gains/losses on loans. MS states that gains/losses for 'Loans and Other assets-Other investments' are classified in 'Other revenues'. GS reports that gains/losses from changes in fair value of loans held for investment (under the fair value option) are included in 'other principal transactions'. Both entities record these non-interest income items in revenue-like line items rather than 'Other expenses' or Interest Income, although the specific line item names ('Other revenues' vs. 'other principal transactions') differ based on the bank's reporting structure. Additionally, GS notes the amounts were not material in 2024, whereas MS does not quantify the materiality in the cited text.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Treatment of DVA and Materiality of Realized Gains
comparisons.peer_summary: Unrealized gains or losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) for elected liabilities are recorded in OCI, while realized gains or losses are recorded in principal transactions revenue. Realized gains or losses from instrument-specific credit risk were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft (MS) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) detail the accounting treatment for fair value adjustments on specific assets/liabilities elected under the fair value option. MS specifies that gains/losses for 'Loans and Other assets-Other investments' are in 'Other revenues'. JPM specifies that unrealized gains/losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) for liabilities are recorded in OCI, while realized gains/losses are recorded in 'principal transactions revenue'. While MS discusses assets (Loans/Other) going to revenue, JPM distinguishes between unrealized (OCI) and realized (Revenue) for liabilities. Both disclosures illustrate how fair value option accounting impacts the income statement through non-interest revenue categories ('Other revenues' for MS, 'principal transactions revenue' for JPM) for realized or specific unrealized components, rather than interest income.
